historical_references.reference: Anifa bint Abd al-Muttalib was an early female convert to Islam and the mother of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the fourth Rashidun Caliph. She is believed to have been the first woman to accept Islam, shortly after her husband, Abu Talib, did so in Mecca.
historical_references.time_period: Pre-Islamic period to early 7th century CE
historical_references.context: Anifa was born into the powerful and influential Banu Hashim clan. Her husband, Abu Talib, was the clan's leader and protector of the Kaaba. They had several children, including Ali, who would become a key figure in early Islamic history.

historical_references.reference: Anifa bint al-Harith al-Qurashiyyah was a wife of Umar ibn al-Khattab, the second Rashidun Caliph. She is known for her piety and dedication to Islam. According to some sources, Umar married her to gain her knowledge and wisdom, as she was a learned woman and a descendant of the Prophet Muhammad's uncle, Abu Talib.
historical_references.context: Umar ibn al-Khattab was a respected military commander and the second Rashidun Caliph. He played a crucial role in the expansion of the Islamic empire during the Ridda Wars and the conquest of Egypt. Anifa bint al-Harith was a prominent figure in the early Muslim community and was known for her piety and her deep knowledge of Islamic traditions and history.
